issues: Subject clarity failed: intake does not define one clear manufactured object.
Abstract drift risk is elevated: intake does not sufficiently lock object-first behavior.
fixes: Set subject.type to a manufactured object class and name the exact object in subject.identity.
Add anti-drift rules and explicit bans on texture-only, atmosphere-first, and abstract-first outcomes.

revised_intake.creative_intent: Normalize the user's request for minimal transformation and exact form lock into a material study focused on a clean matte B4C technical ceramic read, preserving the original manufactured object's silhouette and identity.

must_have: exactly one manufactured object as the clear subject
visible contour evidence such as edge, rim, bevel, seam, or curvature
material visibly attached to the object, not floating as texture
visible edge, rim, bevel, seam, or contour evidence
material visibly attached to the object

composition.framing: centered, clear view of the single manufactured object
composition.background: minimal, non-distracting, solid color or subtle gradient

constraints: uniform illumination to reveal surface texture
color must remain subordinate to material identity
color must follow form then material, never override them
no flat color, always material texture variation
pure white and pure black are forbidden
ceramic off-white must stay warm and broken, never sterile pure white
charcoal black must keep temperature variation, never dead pure black
restrained crimson only in seams, cores, or controlled heat accents
muted earth support only, low saturation material support tones

core_risks: Abstract composition issues leading to subject loss
Drift towards texture-only or atmosphere-first outcomes
Material misinterpretation (e.g., glossy plastic instead of matte ceramic)
material misread as plaster, stone, or glossy plastic
anti_drift_rules: Lock the object read to a single, clearly defined manufactured object
Prevent abstract drift or atmospheric dominance
Ensure continuous, readable contour evidence of the subject
Strictly suppress any reads of plaster, gypsum, chalk, concrete, carved stone, mineral drift, glossy plastic, PVC sheen, or toy-like finish
Maintain material-only scope without losing the manufactured object read
always preserve one clearly readable manufactured object
do not let texture or atmosphere become the subject
keep material identity locked and explicit
form -> material -> color priority is mandatory
do not allow neon, pure white, pure black, or plastic-clean RGB drift
crimson may appear only as restrained seam/core accent when applicable
do not allow abstract, texture-only, or atmosphere-first subject drift
keep material identity explicit and stable
success_criteria: Immediate and unambiguous identification of a single manufactured object
Clean, matte B4C technical ceramic material read
Dry, dense, engineered surface finish clearly visible
Preservation of the original shape and silhouette
image does not collapse into abstract texture or atmosphere
color feels subtractive and pigment-like, never RGB-clean
shadow mass dominates and color remains materially grounded
image does not read as plaster, stone, or glossy plastic
revised_intake.direction_summary: Focus on rendering a single, clearly identifiable manufactured object with a clean matte B4C technical ceramic material. Ensure the surface is dry, dense, and engineered, explicitly avoiding forbidden material reads. Maintain the original shape and silhouette, preventing any abstract drift or loss of subject identity. The composition should be a clear ENTITY_MEDIUM shot with even lighting to highlight the material properties.
